articleTitle: Mitigating System Imbalance Using Enhanced Droop Control in Decentralized Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Power imbalance poses a significant challenge in decentralized microgrids because of the dynamic nature of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and varying load conditions. Conventional voltage droop control methods, while effective in maintaining voltage stability, may not adequately address voltage imbalances caused by unevenly distributed loads or variable generation profiles. This research investigates the implementation of enhanced voltage, power and frequency droop control strategies to mitigate voltage, power and frequency imbalances in decentralized microgrids. The study focuses on optimizing the droop control parameters and integrating supplementary control mechanisms to achieve improved voltage, power and frequency regulation and distribution among DERs. Simulation-based analysis and experimental validation will be conducted to assess the performance and effectiveness of the proposed enhanced voltage, power, and frequency droop control approach in diverse microgrid scenarios. The proposed system has balanced by droop controller within 0.1 to 0.3 sec. This finding provides valuable insights into mitigating voltage, power, and frequency imbalance challenges, enhancing microgrid stability, and ensuring reliable operation of decentralized energy systems.

articleTitle: Designing Nth Level Inverter Using Asymmetric H-bridge MLI Topology: with Techniques to Minimize THD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The Asymmetrical H-Bridge (ASHB) Multilevel Inverter (MLI) is a sophisticated power electronics device that has received great attention for its potential to deliver high-power conversion with decreased harmonic distortion. In this paper, we present a comprehensive investigation of the Asymmetrical H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter, focusing on its operational principles, unique structure, and inherent advantages over conventional two-level inverters. We shall elucidate the architectural configuration of the Asymmetrical H-bridge multilevel Inverter. This configuration comprises a series of cascaded H-bridge modules, each endowed with the capacity to produce numerous discrete voltage levels. This in turn results leading to an improved voltage output resolution. We propose a generalized pattern to construct the N$^{th}$ level of the Asymmetrical H-Bridge Multilevel Inverter, enabling engineers to synthesize higher-level inverters tailored to specific application requirements. The equation takes into account the number of H-bridge modules necessary for the desired level and ensures precise voltage level generation. Additionally, we present a novel approach targeted at mitigating Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). Our proposed approach includes two distinct techniques, and one of the pivotal components is the introduction of a proposed voltage ratio. As a direct outcome, we found a substantial reduction in the THD, attaining an exceptional value of 2.89% across a spectrum encompassing 39 discrete voltage levels. A comprehensive investigation of the THD is undertaken, emphasizing the Asymmetrical H-bridge multilevel Inverter’s capacity to attain low THD values, which considerably improves the output voltage waveform.

articleTitle: A String Current Based Solar PV Array Fault Detection Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Line-to-line or line-to-ground faults are the most common types of PV array faults. In contrast to faults in a power grid, which typically lead to very high currents, faults in a PV system do not necessarily lead to high currents, as these depend on the solar irradiance and the location of the fault. Therefore, fault detection in PV systems becomes a challenging task. The presence of series blocking diodes in a PV system connected in series in parallel makes fault detection with conventional PV array protection devices almost impossible. During partial shading, a solar PV system may exhibit characteristics similar to a fault and vice versa. Therefore, actual fault may go undetected and potentially leads to fire hazard.In this work, a fault detection technique based on monitoring array voltage and string currents is proposed. This technique can detect faults in a series-parallel configured (SPC) PV array, even when the strings are connected with series blocking diodes. A PV array system is developed using MATLAB SIMULINK, where the proposed algorithm is implemented. Simulation results from various faults and partial shading cases justify the applicability of the proposed fault detection algorithm.

articleTitle: A Unified Control for a Soft-Switched Dual Active Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The Dual Active Bridge (DAB) is an isolated converter topology that uses a transformer to offer step-up/step-down capability as well as galvanic isolation for the converter. This DAB Converter has intrinsically zero voltage switching (ZVS) capability, but in a very limited power range, if operated in traditional control mode. The ZVS range of different control techniques namely Phase-shift modulation (PSM), single pulse-width modulation (SPWM), and dual pulse-width modulation (DPWM) control modes for different power ranges have been estimated in this paper in an updated and simpler manner. Three different variables: the phase shift between the primary and secondary transformer voltages, the primary voltage width, and the secondary voltage width are used here to manipulate these control schemes. A hardware prototype of a 600W DAB converter using Silicon MOSFET has been designed and developed to operate at 100 kHz switching frequency amalgamating with three control strategies as mentioned above. The performance of the DAB converter has been initially estimated through mathematical analysis and computer simulations in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Design Aspects of an Electric Vehicle Test-bed for Hybrid-Source Three-wheeler Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Three-wheeled electric vehicles are utilized in the Indian transportation ecosystem as a last-mile connectivity solution. The electrical drive system in these vehicles uses primarily three-phase motors which are powered from a single battery energy storage system. In order to reduce range anxiety, hybrid power sources have been considered for powering these vehicles. A typical arrangement consists of roof-mounted solar panel(s) which act as the secondary power source within the system to provide additional mileage. This paper presents the design aspects of a hybrid source three-wheeler power system considering solar panel and battery as the two sources. The electric vehicle testbed is developed to emulate the on-road behavior of the vehicle using a DC-generator which is mechanically coupled to the drive motor. The dynamic loading on the motor is emulated using a programmable load which is interfaced to the DC generator using a current programmed controlled DC-DC converter. The modeling, design, and analysis of the complete system along with its different sub-systems are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Unveiling the capacitive sensor performance developed for Epicatechin detection in Green tea: A Clustering Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In this present treatise, a selective and economical capacitive sensor performance study has been presented using an unsupervised clustering method. The sensor response, derived from a capacitive sensor modified with a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP), was analyzed using two popular clustering algorithms: K-Means and Agglomerative clustering. To measure the clustering efficacy of the sensor, Silhouette, and Davies-Bouldin scores were employed in this work. The maximum Silhouette scores achieved were 0.8568 and 0.8465 for the two algorithms respectively, with corresponding minimum Davies-Bouldin scores of 0.2016 and 0.2013. These outcomes demonstrate the sensor's proficiency in discerning EC content differences among the green tea samples.

articleTitle: Self-Attention Based Image Feature Representation for Medical Visual Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering is an emerging field which uses artificial intelligence to effectively combine the multimodal data and generate output. Users interact with the visual data through text to generate answers, which may not always be directly accessible from the image. In this paper, a network has been proposed that aims to generate a comprehensive image feature representation, capturing the most relevant visual information present in the image, which is essential for effectively answering questions. The image features are extracted using Uniform Local Binary Pattern Histogram and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix, which are then combined using the multihead self-attention mechanism obtaining a compact and meaningful representation. This combined representation is further fused with deep features to get the desired image feature embedding. Multimodal fusion of the image and text feature embeddings generated the final representation required for the downstream task of Visual Question Answering.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Photoplethysmograph Signals from Noises with Desired Heart and Respiration Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Measurement of various kind of physiological parameters from the photoplethysmograph (PPG) signal has become an emerging area of research in recent years. Hence different state of the art deep learning algorithms are proposed in this domain. But the main problem of using such algorithms is scarcity of biomedical data of the target domain. Thus to alleviate such problems in this paper a novel method of synthesizing PPG data with required variance and desired heart rate (HR) and respiration rate (RR) is proposed. A deep CNN-LSTM autoencoder has been proposed which attempts to reduce an error having three components, targeting to match the morphology with desired variance with the template PPG, HR and RR with the required values. Over 600 samples were generated from the accelerometer noises and yielded a very good result in terms of HR, RR tracking, measured in terms of Mean absolute error (MAE) and KL Divergence, to find out the variance.

articleTitle: A Cost Effective Operation Scheduling of a Solar PV-Biogas-Wind-Grid Integrated Microgrid Considering PV Soiling Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In scheduling the operation of a renewable integrated microgrid, stochasticity of renewable sources and load is generally considered. In solar photovoltaic (SPV) source PV soiling causes substantial loss in generation which is variable and dependent on the environmental parameters like solar radiation, ambient temperature, pressure, wind speed and direction, relative humidity (RH) and precipitation at the place of the plant. This variable loss in generation, save and except radiation, needs to be considered in the operation schedule of the microgrid. In this paper, a physics-based model for PV soiling is used to predict the generation loss, on the basis of which a novel energy management system is devised. The effects of cleaning of SPV plant along with the pre-estimation and inclusion of soiling loss on the sharing of different sources in a microgrid are explicitly demonstrated, leading to a cost-effective operation of the system. The proposition is validated in the field condition in a microgrid at IIEST, Shibpur, consisting of a rooftop SPV power plant (SPVPP), wind generator, biogas generator and grid. The results obtained are presented in the text and are encouraging.

articleTitle: Design of a Weather Adoptive and Traffic Adoptive Wireless LED Street Light Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The aim of this work is to present an intelligent street lighting control scheme that combines real-time measured data from temperature & and humidity sensor and object identification sensors based on radar to generate light control signals which in turn drive spectrally tunable LED streetlights. Application of the proposed scheme will improve the visibility, safety, and energy efficiency of installed street lighting systems in various urban situations through extensive data analysis and data collection depending on the prevailing ambient conditions which will lead to significant contributions to sustainable street lighting methods that are beneficial to both the environment and the community. The working of the proposed scheme has been experimentally tested by developing a prototype model.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effectiveness of Optimization with Modified Stability Boundary Locus Fitting for Approximation of α-order Fractional Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for the rational approximation of fractional-order lowpass and highpass filters of order $\alpha$, where $\alpha \in(0, 1)$. The proposed approach considers the modified stability boundary locus (M-SBL) based filter approximants as an initial point for a classical optimizer to determine the model coefficients. The performance of the M-SBL fitting for the fractional-order filter approximation is compared with the proposed method to justify the effectiveness of the suggested scheme regarding both the magnitude and phase characteristics. The distinct advantage of the proposed approach is to avoid the incorporation of stability and minimum-phase constraints, thus reducing the computational burden. Comparisons with the published literature demonstrate the overall improved frequency-domain fitting performance for the proposed approximants.

articleTitle: On Non-Integer Order Internal Model Control of Non-Minimum Phase Systems and Plants with Transport Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In this work, Internal Model control (IMC) based on fractional order (FO) controller is designed for non-minimum phase (NMP) plants and time delayed system which is also a NMP having a right half plane (RHP) zero which is contributed by the delay itself. An integer order (IO) PID controller is positioned in cascade with the FO filter. The resulting controller is fractional having very interesting structure for its implementation. It is formulated based on satisfactory attainment of the frequency domain design specifications, the impact of which is verified considering the transient parameters of settling time, percentage overshoot and undershoot to determine the controller effectiveness. It is further examined that FO-IMC attains all the response and loop criteria in better extent in contrast to IO-IMC which in all the cases compromises loop over response or vice-verse. (135 Words)

articleTitle: General Type-2 Fuzzy Reasoning for Path-Planning of a Mobile Robot in a Dynamic Environment under Sensory Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Memberships assigned by an expert to different values of a linguistic variable in a classical (Type-1) fuzzy set are crisp. A Type-2 Fuzzy membership function is a union of several Type-1 membership functions obtained from different experts. Type-2 membership at a given value of a linguistic variable is thus fuzzy. Traditional path-planning problem of a mobile robot in a static environment includes Type-1 (sensory) uncertainty due to the angular spacing betweeneach pairs of consecutive ultrasonic sensors mounted around the body of the robot. Type-2 uncertainty appears in path-planning problems due to the presence of moving obstacles in the robot’s workspace. Membership functions used for handling type-1 sensory uncertainty are inadequate to handle type-2 uncertainty in a dynamic environment. This paper introduces a novel algorithm for automated reasoning with the help of a vertical structured General Type-2 version of fuzzy sets, and extends it for trajectory-planning of a mobile robot in presence of dynamic obstacles. A set of 7 benchmark workplaces is used to test the performance of the proposed algorithm, taking specular reflection and multipath effect of sonar transducer into consideration. It is noted that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing techniques with respect to path length and computational overhead.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fitness Adaptive Differential Evolution Approach for Tuning of PID Controller in AVR System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: To upgrade the dynamic performance of the Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR), several control strategies have been implemented by control engineers. The Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller is the most widely used among all the controllers that have been reported. In order to enhance the AVR system’s dynamic performance, this work addresses the design of a PID controller utilizing a unique optimization technique known as the Enhanced Fitness Adaptive Differential Evolution Algorithm (EFADE). The EFADE algorithm demonstrates an excellent robustness in calculating the PID controller parameters. Time domain response and frequency domain response specifications are evaluated to validate the efficacy of the designed controller. Results reveal an improved dynamic response along with superior load disturbance rejection performance for the proposed EFADE-PID controller as compared to the recently published literature.

Author Keywords: enhanced fitness adaptive differential evolution algorithm

articleTitle: Multi-Feature Enhancement of Standard and Modified A-star and RRT Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This manuscript suggests improvements in offline path planning algorithms: A-star (A*) and Rapidly Exploring Random Trees (RRT)-well-celebrated algorithms for robot path planning. The conventional algorithm of A* is reliable for path length efficiency, while RRT focuses on relaxing computation complexity. Specifically, this work aims to introduce three feature enhancements: bi-directionality, obstacle padding, and smoothing—to improve the capability of traditional algorithms. These enhancements have been applied to A*, a modified version of RRT, and the jump-point search (JPS) variant of A*. A comparative study is presented for the path-planning of a non-holonomic autonomous mobile robot to assess the effectiveness of these modified algorithms with augmented features. The simulations were conducted using MATLAB, where a configuration space with multiple obstacles is considered. Finally, insights into the advantages offered by these enhancements and their impact on the performance of the algorithms have been discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Multi-cell VLC System and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Connecting the dots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The several advantages of visible light communication (VLC) have made it a potentially competent candidate for future communication technology. The reliability of the VLC system depends on the line-of-sight (LOS) links. However, surrounding environments pose unique challenges, frequently causing LOS blockages. The reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) also known as intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) is a collection of tunable passive elements that have proven their ability in RF communication to manipulate and control the transmitted/reflected RF signals by changing the orientation or phases of RIS. RIS is anticipated to play a crucial role in enhancing VLC by shadowing compensation, extending coverage by controlling the beam directions and improving communication reliability by mitigating interferences. This work delves into the emerging field of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and their transformative role in multi-cell indoor visible light communication (VLC) systems. A RIS-based indoor multi-cell system model is developed for the purpose of mitigating inter-channel interference (ICI) issues during LOS blockages. The SINR performance of the proposed system is estimated for four different scenarios. Results show that the integration of RIS in between VLC channels can enhance the detector’s received power up to 27 times compared to the power received from the LOS and NLOS channels. Moreover, incorporating RIS has raised the average SINR value by 25% during no blockage and more than 70.4% during the blockage.

articleTitle: A Voltammetric Study for Amaranth Detection Using Carbon Paste Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper summarizes an investigating work on a simple and budget-friendly Carbon Paste Electrode (CPE) for finding Amaranth (AMR). AMR is one of the fabricated colorants applied significantly to enhance the attractiveness and look of various foodstuffs and drinks. However, immoderate AMR intake may result in severe health hazards. Naturally, the accurate determination of AMR content in food is necessary. Both Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) and Differential Pulse Voltammetry (DPV) techniques have been employed to evaluate the electrochemical behavior of this CPE using Phosphate buffer (PBS 6) as the supporting electrolyte. The recorded data proves this electrode to be an effective one in determining AMR in various concentrations in a range of 5-100 $\mu$M with a satisfactory limit of detection (LOD) of 0.17 $\mu$M; and excellent repeatability, reproducibility and stability with Relative Standard Deviation (RSD) of 1.1%, 2.8%, and 2.6% respectively. This newly developed electrode thus can be used in rapid detection of AMR.

articleTitle: Investigating EMG Fatigue Markers of Biceps Muscle: A Comparative Study Through Mono Fractal and Band Power Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Muscle fatigue assessment plays a crucial role in clinical diagnostics for muscle rehabilitation. While numerous conventional methods are available for testing fatigue; their subjective or qualitative nature prevents them from being considered the gold standard. This research strives to offer a deeper comprehension of the complexity and dynamic changes present in muscle activity patterns, as analysed through EMG signals during biceps muscle contractions under different loading conditions. To facilitate the experiment, EMG data of biceps brachii muscle from five volunteers were obtained for 30 seconds duration using a DIY electromyography sensor & surface electrodes equipped with the essential signal acquisition circuitry. The data was subjected to monofractal analysis, where the fractal dimension (D) was determined through Hurst’s exponent (H), and opposite trends were observed across 4Kg & 6Kg loading conditions. In contrast, band power computation is employed to assess the power within distinct frequency bands in EMG signals, offering insights into how muscle activity is distributed across different spectral domains. This approach facilitates the more rapid detection of alterations in muscle activation patterns leading to real-time monitoring of fatigue irrespective of diverse loading conditions, and showcasing its superiority over monofractal analysis.

articleTitle: Classroom Automation & Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In the era of advanced technology, students as well as teachers are more demanding innovative university campus life. Technologies like IoT and Cloud computing can provide solutions for smart and a sustainable campus toupgrade manual/traditional methods and improve the efficiency of everyday activities in the Institution. For example, automated attendance system used to track students who are not regular or skip theirclasses, send alerts to parents and students helps to concentrate academic work regularly and it also reduces the stress of parents. It also monitors the COVID-19 Protocol. Hence, the purpose of the paper is to introduce a system of automation to monitor various activities in a classroom and to keep a track of the activities hence making it globally accessible using IoT and cloud features so that any responsible authority can access the data for meaningful insight.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive Control of Time Delay Plant in 2-DoF Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Systems with time delay in various configurations are very common in the engineering systems and they pose various challenges during the control systems design. This paper presents the design of a control system for an inherently unstable plant with time delay component. Padè approximation of the time delay component exhibits right hand plane (RHP) zero leads to Non-Minimum Phase (NMP) characteristics, which obstruct the stabilization as well as perfect tracking of the time delay system. Here, the feed-forward Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) technique for the inverse plant model and the State Feedback (SFB) Control scheme as feedback compensation for the non-inverse plant model are designed in a two degree of freedom (2-DoF) framework to obtain the stable and good tracking performance of the above-said unstable plant. The performance of the proposed control algorithm has been verified for 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order plant with their time delay component in the MATLAB SIMULINK environment and compared their dynamic responses with the SFB control technique.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Proportional Integral Derivative driven Frequency Compensation of Grid-connected AC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Integration of renewable energy sources into the microgrid impacts Load Frequency Control (LFC) negatively. So, an effective solution to tackle the problem of LFC with RES in microgrid is needed. In this paper, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithms (GA) are used to optimize the Proportional-Integral-Derivative (Three-term) gain constants for a single-area control system. When the traditional PID is implemented, this leads to the ordinary controller failing to modify the AGC. To optimize the three-term controller variables using PSO and GA. The method applies to single-area systems. The outcomes demonstrate how precisely and reliably the optimized controller variables were implemented. The performance of PSO and GA are also compared with Ziegler Nichols’s method of tuning PID parameters and Conventional PI controller. System equations are solved with MATLAB Simulation. When compared to a traditional controller, the optimized controller that has been suggested exhibits faster response times and higher control quality.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Assessment of Educational Institutions in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Efficient use of energy and its saving is essential to balance the energy demand-supply scenario as well as sustainable development of a country. In this paper, energy audit is used to assess energy management system of a commercial building housing a Department of a University in Dhaka city. The various components of the building such as building envelop, energy use profile, electrical appliances for example, air conditioning system, lighting system have been analyzed. It has been found that air conditioning system consumes 58.34% of total power supply while lighting system represents only 2.34%. Considering the functionality of air conditioning and lighting system in the building, targeted energy audits had been carried out on them. The potential energy savings and cost-benefit are calculated and evaluated for proposed interventions in the systems. Result shows that 38.61% and 68.61% energy could be saved from lighting and air conditioning system respectively with payback period of 2.1 years for lighting system and 8 years for air conditioning system.

articleTitle: A novel relative entropy based FCM algorithm using interval type-2 fuzzy set at local membership functions for brain MR image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In this proposed article, we develop a fuzzy c-means algorithm based on relative entropy for segmentation of noisy volumetric brain MR images and introduce interval type-2 fuzzy membership functions by using local membership functions as a secondary membership function. The brain magnetic resonance images are influenced by high level of intensity inhomogeneity (IIH) and noise, because of the limitations of machinery devices and cognitive limitations of the operators. As a result it produces blurry images, mostly at the soft tissue boundary regions. This phenomenon increases uncertainty for the image soft tissue classification. The proposed algorithm handle this issue by incorporating interval type-2 fuzzy (IT2F) set at the local membership functions to reduce the underlying uncertainty factors of each voxels more efficiently. It also integrates the total uncertainties for volumetric images by utilizing relative entropy. At first, the proposed algorithm generates the global and local membership functions for each voxel, next, it generates type-2 fuzzy (T2F) set by considering local membership functions as a secondary membership functions and finally, the algorithm generates IT2F set by doing direct defuzzificaton of the T2F set. We conduct qualitative and quantitative experiments on ten different simulated volumes of brain MR images. The results revel the outcome of the experiments and it indicates the supremacy of the proposed algorithm over the state-of-the-art algorithms established in near past.

articleTitle: Band gap Analysis of Undoped and Doped Photo anode for Dye Sensitized Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) have amassed conspicuous contemplation as a convalescent anomalous to traditional solar cells due to their tending cost-effectiveness and capability for efficient light harvesting. Titanium dioxide $(TiO_{2})$, as photo anode, a widely used semiconducting material in DSSCs, plays a pivotal role in electron transport and charge separation processes. In this study, the effects and performance of doped and undoped titanium dioxide in DSSCs has been investigated. Undoped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> serves as the reference material, providing a benchmark for comparison with doped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The introduction of 0.1% Magnesium (Mg) dopant aims to enhance the photoelectric properties of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by attuning its band gap, charge carrier concentration, and charge transport properties. The hydrothermal synthesis fabrication technique is used for both undoped and doped Titanium dioxide films. The morphological characteristic is analyzed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with particle size of Undoped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to be 67nm and 0.1% Magnesium doped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to be 59nm. The optical properties of the films are pored over through techniques such as UV-Vis spectroscopy. Doping influences the light absorption range and optical bandgap of Titanium dioxide, thereby affecting the overall photo conversion efficiency. Undoped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> shown the bandgap to be 3.59 nm and Mg doped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to be 3.51 nm.The results demonstrate that doping TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> can significantly augment the efficiency of DSSCs by improving light absorption, reducing charge recombination, and enhancing charge carrier transport. This study provides valuable apprehensions into the impact of Magnesium doping on the properties of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in DSSCs and highlights the potential for further optimization of dopant types and concentrations to maximize the efficiency of dyesensitized solar cells. The findings contribute to the ongoing efforts in developing advanced materials for Dye Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSCs).

articleTitle: Design of an improved Fractional Order PID controller using Variable Set-Point Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel control strategy for Fractional Order PID (FOPID) controllers i.e., Variable Set-Point Weighted Variable Fractional Order PID (VSPWVFOPID) controller. To implement this control scheme, three different values of set-point weighting factor ($\beta$), integral order ($\lambda$) and differential order ($\mu$) are selected for three different regions of output response and applied to set-point, integral action, and differential action, respectively. The key focus of this control scheme is to provide satisfactory results in both, initial transient and load rejection phases as well as superior robust control. The effectiveness of the proposed VSPW-VFOPID controller is demonstrated considering two different process models and their 10% perturbed systems in MATLAB simulation platform. The performance of the proposed control scheme is compared with existing control techniques like Ziegler Nichols (ZN) tuning, Fixed Set Point Weighting (FSPW), Variable Set Point Weighting (VSPW), and Fractional Order PID (FOPID). In this context, VSPW-VFOPID can provide better response during both phases. For the purpose of this paper, various performance indices are considered like Percentage Overshoot (OS%), Rise-Time $(\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{r}})$, Peak-Time $(\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{p}})$, Settling-Time $(\mathrm{t}_{\mathrm{s}})$, Integral Absolute Error (IAE), Integral Square Error (ISE), and Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE). From the results of the proposed scheme, it can be concluded that, apart from enhanced robust control, VSPW-VFOPID shows excellent performance during initial set-point tracking and load rejection phases which makes it superior to other existing control schemes.

articleTitle: A study on fault diagnosis in solar photovoltaic array using artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Timely detection, diagnosis and mitigation of short-circuit and arcing faults are essential to avoid catastrophic damage and service discontinuity of solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays. In this work, an application of artificial neural network (ANN) is demonstrated for the fast and accurate diagnosis of string fault, string-to-ground fault and string-to-string fault in a 250 kW grid-tied solar PV array. The electrical features are chosen based on information gain ratio and the model hyperparameters are set based on random search optimization. It is observed that the ANN model displays high classification accuracies for the training (100%), validation (100%) and testing (98%) data; small generalization error (0.02) and fast training speed (7s). Most of these indices are improved compared to the earlier works. Such a smart fault-detection scheme can be deployed physically in a solar power plant.

articleTitle: MicroNET: Microarray Image Orientation Predictor and Automated Data Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Microarray is a high-throughput platform consisting of several thousands of DNA, protein, or peptides on a chip surface. In the current scenario, researchers have to use a scanner such as GenePix®4000B to scan such chips. However, after scanning these chips, researchers need to manually adjust the orientation angle of the grid to be placed in the microarray image before moving on to the spot intensity extraction step and data analysis. This paper introduces a novel lightweight deep-learning model, MicroNET, to predict the orientation angle and top left coordinates of the grid. After the image is corrected and the grid is placed, we also perform automatic fluorescence intensity extraction. This paper has compared two different configurations of MicroNET. The first one makes use of a ResNet18 backbone while the next one is a modified version of the ResNet18 backbone with lesser parameters. As per our results, the model with the modified ResNet18 backbone predicts the orientation angle with an MSE of 0.379 and the top left coordinates with an MSE of 0.0011. Thus the model with the modified ResNet18 backbone achieves better results with a lesser number of parameters. Hence it can be easily executed on any microarray data extraction software and will enable researchers to prepare microarray datasets easily.

articleTitle: Prediction of Noise-Type and its Elimination from Photoplethysmograph Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Non-invasive measurement of photoplethysmograph (PPG) signal is an emerging research area. However the presence of noises in such signals may give erroneous interpretations. This paper thus proposes a technique to identify the noise model in the PPG signal, followed by the suitable de-noising techniques. Reservoir computing (RC) model has been used for the classification purpose which reduces numbers of learnable parameters and provided fast training. Cepstrum analysis has been applied for the elimination of convolutive noises. The method has been tested on 700 PPG windows and yielded good results from the point of view of PPG de-noising and estimation of respiration rate (RR) in terms of NRMSE and PCC with a standalone hardware implementation on a low-cost resource-constrained embedded device (Raspberry Pi Zero W) having an end-to-end latency and memory engagement of 165.34 s and 331.10 KB respectively.

articleTitle: Optimised Intelligent Coordination Between Electric Vehicles and Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) have become popular and appealing vehicles due to technological development, environmental issues, and societal considerations. Electrical distribution networks have experienced significant stability, and reliability effects as a result of this trend. EV charging that is unplanned and haphazard can increase power losses, overloads, and extreme voltage deviations, all of which are harmful to the security and dependability of growing smart grids. This study suggests a unique method for organizing the charging schedule of several electric vehicles (EVs) in a smart grid system at a reduced cost and power loss. This study primarily focuses on the power cost with and without time scheduling once the various zones in the system have been identified using the proposed Zone Clustering Index (ZCI). Additionally, power flow and transmission losses have been computed. Particle swarm optimisation (PSO) has been used for cost estimations. Results from testing the suggested approach on a modified IEEE 30 bus system are highly encouraging.

articleTitle: Induction Motor Inter-turn Short Circuit Fault Classification by Extracting Auto Features Using LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Inter Turn Short Circuit (ITSC) fault in stator winding of three phase induction motor (IM) is one of the most recurrent type of failures, which counts more than 30% of total electrical faults in machine. Thus, the investigation of ITSC fault detection in early stage is essential, since IMs are widely used in industries and household applications. The proposed work exploits the facility of deep learning-based approaches for ITSC fault detection in IMs using auto feature extraction enabled Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Neural network. Initially, three phase stator current envelop is extracted by Hilbert Transform and the envelop samples are used further for auto feature extraction. Along with, modified weighted batch normalization (BN) is used to improve the training capability of proposed method. MATLAB/ SIMULINK model with three different IM parameters along with three different loading conditions are used to train the proposed diagnostic system for eight different stator fault conditions. The method is also experimentally tested with 1 hp IM to check the accuracy of the diagnostic system. The performance of proposed method is compared with statistical feature extraction with ANN and from the result, it is observed that auto feature extraction using LSTM neural network is more accurate (up to 98%) than previous one.

articleTitle: Different Cascaded Modified Forms of Fractional Order Compensation for Unstable Non-Minimum Phase Systems and Plants with Transport Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Fractional Order (FO)Lead/lag compensators in its performance are superior and more flexible with its non-integer orders in contrary to the integer order (IO) ones. In the control systems designed in the domain of frequency, phase lead compensation is one of the most commonly used techniques. Desired predefined frequency domain traits with phase which will be maximal at the specified new frequency where the gain plot makes intercepts or cross-over occurs can be attained accurately with the supplementary parameter, the fractional order of this new form of lead compensator. Therefore, here in this work, a solution of this compensator pole-zero locations dependent on its different corner frequencies which are exact and unique with the additional parameters in its generalized form is deliberated with MATLAB simulated results on some practical numerical examples adopted.(132 Words)

articleTitle: Classification of Green Tea Samples Based on Epigallocatechin-3-Gallate Content Using Molecular Imprinting Polymerization Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The proposed system implements a machine learning based approach to classify samples of green tea based on the EGCG (Epigallocatechin-3-Gallate) content. The EGCG content in green tea samples are estimated by using the synthesized molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) electrode. The voltametric responses were obtained using a three-electrode set-up. The data was recorded and pre-processed. The responses obtained after pre-processing are fed for feature selection using UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) algorithm, in which the number of features is reduced to generate optimized output. Further, the selected features are processed with K-means clustering method, to distinguish the green tea samples. The classification of green tea samples is performed by using XGBoost (Extreme Gradient Boost) algorithm. The use of XGBoost provides fast converging with limited steps, direct route to the least error and simplified calculations to lower computational costs and improve speed. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed system is calculated based on metrics namely, Calinski Harabasz Score, Distortion score and Silhouette score for K-means clustering technique. The efficiency of the introduced XGBoost method is calculated based on the metrics such as accuracy, AUC (Area under Curve), Recall, Precision, F1-score, Kappa and MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient) with outcomes of 0.96, 0.99, 0.96, 0.96, 0.96, 0.94 and 0.95. Thus, the outcome of the proposed method denotes the effective performance in classifying the green tea samples.

articleTitle: LFC of DFIG-Wind Farm Incorporated Multimachine Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: As the fossil fuel resources are diminishing rapidly, renewable energy generation and its penetration in power system is the trend in the modern era. In large multimachine power systems, as penetration of renewable energy units like wind energy are increasing day by day, load frequency control (LFC) issue is posing a serious challenge to the power system engineers due to fluctuating nature of the wind. Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind energy generating units being popular due to its capability of harnessing its stored kinetic energy, in the present work, such units are incorporated in all the three areas of 39-Bus New England Power System, separated by a deterministic method considering the power sharing of generators, for LFC study of the system. Furthermore, a latest Fuzzy technique i.e. Fuzzy-tuned PID Controllers (FT-PIDC) are used as LFC controllers and its performance is compared with conventional PID controllers (PIDC) in the LFC study of the DFIG-integrated system. Parameters of FT-PIDC and PIDC are optimized by Multi-objective Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (MOGHOA).

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis on Application of PI and LQR Based Control for Speed Tracking of a DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: DC motors have found extensive industrial usage due to their wide range of speed control and excellent speed torque characteristics. The simplest speed control technique for dc motor is the proportional integral (PI) control due to its ease of implementation since all the control variables are dc quantities. Improved performance can be achieved by using other control techniques like deadbeat control, fuzzy logic control, model predictive control and state feedback control. The optimal control approach of state feedback is Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control which has been proven to achieve better control action compared to classical control approaches. This paper emphasizes on the mathematical approach to design the LQR controller for speed control of a DC motor by converting the reference tracking problem into a regulator problem. The controller has been designed in the Simulink environment of MATLAB and the performance of the designed controller is compared to that of a PI based controller.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant V formation control of a leader-follower based multi-robot system in an unknown occluded environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-organized flocking algorithm for a multi-robot system that employs the traditional leader-follower approach to produce and maintain V formation while navigating toward an objective location. To achieve self-organization for mimicking the bird flocking characteristics, a circular region-based shaped control strategy followed by an equilateral triangle fitting scheme is described. The control logic has been devised in such a manner that the multi-robot system can orient its inter-agent formation along the direction of the incoming navigational path. The system also includes a fault-tolerant feature in which, if the leader agent becomes weary during navigation, it will be automatically replaced by its immediate follower agent, mimicking the self-healing function of the bird flocking schemes. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed technique, simulation results (with and without fault-tolerant aspect) are furnished in this article.

articleTitle: Brain-Actuated Speed Modulation for Position Control of an Artificial Robotic Limb for Rehabilitative Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The paper provides a novel approach to design and develop a brain-actuated 2-loop position control with an inner loop to control speed and an outer loop to control position of an artificial robotic limb for neuro-motor rehabilitation. The subject utilizes motor imagery brain signal to drive the robotic limb-motor at a fixed speed until he finds the limb crossing the desired target position. The subject releases an ErrP brain signal, when the robotic limb crosses the target position first time. The brain-computer interface system recognizes the target position by identifying the location on the trajectory of the robot arm, at the instance when ErrP is released by the subject. The position of the robot arm at the said instance corresponds to zero-crossing in positional error. Depending on reaction-time of the subject in releasing ErrP, the positional offset-error usually has a non-zero (variable) magnitude, which needs corrections by the subsequent mode of automatic control. The brain-actuated speed-modulator sets the speed of the limb to half of its value after each zero-crossing, however, with an opposite sign. Novelty of the work lies in brain-actuated controller design and stability analysis of the system using Root Locus theory. The merit of the proposed scheme lies in reduced cognitive load of the subject as he is set free after releasing the ErrP at the first zero-crossing of positional error.

articleTitle: Bamboo-based solar powered garden light as eco-friendly and sustainable outdoor lighting solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Research and innovations in the fields of renewable energy and sustainable design have been sparked by the need for sustainable and environmentally friendly energy solutions. This research paper describes the design, fabrication, and performance assessment of a bamboo-based solar garden light that operates a 1W led load from dusk to dawn while being charged by a 3W solar panel. Incorporating solar energy and bamboo as a structural and aesthetically pleasing material demonstrates how traditional craftsmanship and cutting-edge technology can coexist harmoniously to produce an environmentally friendly outdoor lighting solution. The solar garden lights are made from treated bamboos, which make them resistant to insects and varying weather condition. A month-long performance evaluation study for the fabricated solar garden light is carried out, giving a satisfactory result.

articleTitle: Sensorless BLDC Motor Tracking Control using EMRAS Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The prime objective of this article is to justify a novel type of controller as Enhanced Model Reference Adaptive System (EMRAS) controller for the tracking control of sensor less BLDC motor. The application of this novel form of controller to BLDC drives is discussed in this study, along with a discussion of the key changes in the implementation with relation to speed tracking, rising time, and overshoot. Commutation of BLDC motor is accomplished by the back emf estimation method which follows zero cross detector (ZCD) to substitute the effectivity of hall sensors. The findings of simulations and experiments demonstrate that, when compared to the traditional PI control, EMRAS control produces less torque ripple and a faster tracking response with a low rising time and nearly no overshoot.

articleTitle: Solution of thermal-solar integrated economic load dispatch problems using chaos assisted backtracking search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In terms of producing pollution-free power, renewable energy has recently had a considerable impact on the power generation industry. In this study, traditional economic load dispatch (ELD) problems are solved by integrating thermal with solar power plants to reduce generation cost of generated demand power. Here, chaos-based backtracking search algorithm (CBSA) has been used to determine optimal generation cost of traditional ten, fifteen and forty unit thermal power generation. CBSA has been also applied to reduced generation cost of three separated thermal-solar test systems - one solar-ten thermal, one solar-fifteen thermal and one solar-forty thermal. Proposed generation model can be able to reduce generation cost (i.e., 22278${\$}$, 3027${\$}$ and 4664${\$}$) from the generation cost of traditional generation model. Proposed results show the effectiveness of the presented thermal-solar generation models than traditional generation models. The efficacy of the suggested CBSA has been demonstrated by comparing the generating costs of different test systems to the outcomes of other applied algorithms, such as the BSA, COVID 19, and whale algorithms.

articleTitle: Traction Locomotive Incipient Fault Analysis using Wavelet based Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The present work aspires to pursue a qualitative research on the loosening of brushes in Indian induction motor locomotives, observing the traction transformer input current. At the initial step, the locomotive has been built in programming and the current input to the transformer has been documented at normal condition. Brushes have been gradually loosened and the transformer inputs have again been recorded. Both the currents have been assessed using a novel Wavelet Transform (WT) coefficient statistical analysis based Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) Technique. From the computed Skewness, Kurtosis and RMS values, global bests have been disintegrated and optimization has been done in PSO plane to assess different conditions in the engine associated with an incipient brush fault. Here multi-objective PSO (MOPSO) has been used for the assessment and decision making. With the outcome of the refinement, a credo has been developed at the end to segregate the faulty traction engine from the healthy one. The technique used here has been validated in offline mode with satisfactory outcome.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Surface Based Reflecting Screens for Improving Indoor Wireless Communication.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: A dual band stop resistive type frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented in this paper for enhancing wireless signal coverage in indoor environments. The main problem of the passive FSS is when once it has been designed practically, it does not allow the duplicate or other different frequency behavior from it. To get rid of this important problem, the use of active elements (like PIN diode, Varactor diode, LDR) in the FSS is a very useful solution. FSS loaded by LDR is considered as reconfigurable surface to the EM wave dependent on intensity of light incident on it. The intensity of the light changes the resistance value of the LDR and thus the induced current path resistance varies. Here the effect of the resistance value in the induced current path of the FSS is being discussed in the article. The unit cell of the proposed FSS consists of two concentric square ring-shaped patches. Four resistive elements are loaded on each square ring. The effect of the variation in the resistance values of these elements on the transmission characteristics of the FSS is studied in detail. The proposed FSS shows dual band stop characteristics at 2.4 GHz and 4.95 GHz. By changing the resistance values $(0.1 \Omega, 10 \Omega, 50 \Omega$ and $100 \Omega)$ of the resistive elements in the inner and outer loop of the proposed design a tunable behavior of the frequency characteristics of the proposed design has been achieved. Reflective screens based on the proposed design can be used on building walls for improving wireless communication in complex indoor environments.

articleTitle: Influence of Buffer Length and Mole Fraction on Analog Performances of a Symmetrical Underlapped DG Si/SiGe-based MOS-HEMT Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The Authors through this paper have investigated and performed an in-depth study of the Analog performances of an Underlapped Dual Gate (U-DG) Si/SiGe Metal Oxide Semiconductor-High Electron Mobility Transistor (MOS-HEMT) device consisting of HfO2 as a high-k Gate dielectric material. The authors compared the aforementioned device by varying the central Si buffer length sandwiched in between the transcending Silicon Germanium (SiGe) layers and by varying the mole fraction of the SiGe layer. The study focuses on the effect of the conduction band energy profile along with various analog parameters, Drain (Id) and Gate (Ig) Currents, Transconductance (gm), and the Transconductance Generation Factor (TGF). Results show that a buffer length of 30 nm and mole fraction of 0.1 for Si in SiGe gave the best performance. The analysis showed that utilizing a 30 nm buffer length resulted in an increase in Id by a minimum of 41.6% and gm by 1.5% compared to other buffer lengths. Moreover, a mole fraction of 0.1 increases the Id by 4.5% and the gm by 1.9%.

articleTitle: MRMR Guided EMG analysis for Precise Hand Gesture Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Dysfunction and partial loss of movement of hand leads to significant limitation of daily activities in patients after stroke or upper limb amputation. Therapy with the help of rehabilitation devices can assist in restoring motor function which in turn requires real time classification and detection of hand gestures through machine learning algorithms which includes data acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction and classification. Surface electromyography (sEMG) is one of the biomedical signals used to detect the patient’s motor intent from their residual muscles following amputation or stroke. In this paper, our main goal is to classify signals from wrist and forearm muscles for hand gestures: opposition, extension of fingers and wrist, flexion of the wrist, opening and closing of the hand, by feature selection with a novel application of the Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (MRMR) method in EMG. We studied seven existing time-domain features and proposed one new time-domain feature for the purpose of hand gesture identification, namely the squared integral of slope (SIS). Comparative bar graphs were plotted and MRMR was used for the selection of the best features for classification. The following widely used classification techniques of EMG signal are assessed and compared: Bagged trees ensemble, Cubic SVM, and Neural network. With an accuracy of 72.4 percent, the bagged tress ensemble shows good performance in identifying the various hand gestures.

articleTitle: Analysis of Active Power Transfer to Grid from a Specific EV - A V2G Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This proposed work investigates the power transfer from a vehicle to grid (V2G) technology. A specified electric vehicle (EV), e.g., Tata Nexon EV - Prime is considered in which Lithium-Ion (Li-Ion) battery is used. The battery energy storage system (BESS) of the same is studied from its charging and discharging characteristics. A dc-dc converter for boost operation is used to step-up the dc voltage to operate three-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) in synchronous reference frame (SRF), i.e., in dq-domain for injection of active power at grid frequency. An LCL filter is used for rejection of higher frequency components from inverter current to maintain less total harmonic distortion (THD) at lower voltage. A three-phase two-winding power transformer is required to provide isolation and maintained voltage level between grid and inverter.

articleTitle: BER Performance Analysis For Outdoor Wireless Channels Using Low Complexity Neural Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Reduction of channel distortions and the reconstruction of transmitted data is challenging for wireless systems. MIMO OFDM modelling can be used for the wireless channels to analyse the receiver performance. But the receiver performance degrades due to multipath fading effects in wireless channels and the equalizer plays a crucial role for designing the detector for wireless receiver. Low complexity neural network architecture is quite effective for developing adaptive equalization models that can minimize bit errors and enhance the receiver throughput in case of practical channel conditions. The proposed equalization models are tested to reconstruct data stream with minimum bit error. Rayleigh and Nakagami-m models are used to characterize outdoor wireless environment with similar fading statistics. The training of neural equalization models is performed using different variants of LMS algorithms. The BER performance, MSE performance and eye diagram analysis bring a strong point to utilize the proposed adaptive equalizer in MIMO ODFM outdoor channels for optimal data detection.

articleTitle: Impedance Measurement Technique for Vehicle Battery Health Assessment Using On-Board CAN Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Assessing the State of Health (SOH) of on-board battery pack is imperative to ensure optimal vehicle performance and safety. Amongst the non-destructive methods, one approach for calculating SOH involves extracting the battery’s ohmic resistance value. This process is conventionally done with the use of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy in a laboratory setting, necessitating specialized equipment. In this article, we introduce an online impedance measurement technique that utilizes only the existing sensors and accessible controller area network (CAN) bus data from the battery management system in an electric vehicle. The AC harmonics present in standard driving cycles are employed in conjunction with the Fourier transform to generate a Nyquist plot with a frequency range of 10 mHz to 0.5 Hz. The method is tested on three different standard drive schedules and the findings indicate that the ohmic resistance value can be determined from the Nyquist plot using as little as 360 seconds of sensor data sampled at 1 Hz. The value of the ohmic resistance is subsequently validated through the hybrid pulse power characterization (HPPC) test, performed using a state-of-the-art laboratory battery tester. The ohmic resistance value obtained using the proposed methodology exhibits remarkable consistency with that derived from the HPPC test results. A maximum difference of 7.4 percent is observed when a short segment of the drive cycle is employed, which decreases to a maximum of 2.7 percent when the entire drive cycle data is considered.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Hybrid LiFi-RF Network Using Freeform Based Angle Diversity Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: The recent release of the IEEE 802.11bb-2023 global light communication standard opens up exciting opportunities for LiFi-enabled devices to work seamlessly with RF technology. In this study, we extend our previously reported research on freeform-based angle diversity receiver by using it for a multiuser indoor hybrid LiFi-RF framework. The network performances have been investigated in terms of throughput, packet loss ratio and latency. The off-axis quadrilateral field of view of the freeform-based receiver offers excellent resilience against inter-channel interference. The result shows, nearly 300 Mbps average user throughput when 10 users are in motion inside the indoor environment. Moreover, exemplary improvement in overall system throughput has been observed compared to state-of-the-art research in the presence of light-path blockage.

articleTitle: FPA-based Approximation and Realization of Analog Fractional-Order Integrator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper presents the approximation of the analog fractional-order integrator, commonly referred to as the $s^{-\alpha}$ operator, where $\alpha\in (0, 1)$, using a metaheuristic optimization strategy. The minimization of the frequency response error of the biquadratic approximant with respect to the targeted model is carried out using Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA). Five different models are suggested by varying a tuning parameter in the cost function which controls the degree of effort individually expended by FPA on minimizing the magnitude and the phase errors. Comparisons with the current literature justify the improved approximation accuracy of the proposed designs. Circuit implementation for the FPA-based half-order integrator is validated using PSPICE.

articleTitle: A Proficient Cascaded Filter Design for Image Denoising by Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a competent cascaded filter for image denoising using Arithmetic optimization Algorithm (AOA). Though several conventional spatial domain filters are used individually to perform denoising, but fails to give satisfactory results for various types of available noises like Gaussian, Salt & Pepper, and Speckle. Thus, cascading multiple spatial filters by means of AOA algorithm shows upgraded outcome compared to existing methods. The comparative study is carried out among popular spatial filters and the proposed cascaded filter through objective and subjective analysis. The quality measurement parameters like IQI, PSNR, and SSIM shows significant improvement for various noises and upgraded visual attributes in reconstructed image. Furthermore, the comparative graphical investigation of quality parameters for different denoising methods against various noise variance levels shows it is well designed to resist low- and high-density noises. Thus, it is quite apparent that our proposed design provides an optimal solution compared to conventional denoising methods.

articleTitle: V/f Control of PMSM Drive fed from PR Current Controller Based Single-Phase AFE Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: In this proposed work, the performance of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) with open-loop V/f control has been analyzed both in constant torque and constant power region. The supply side is connected through a single-phase Active Front-End (AFE) rectifier to provide dc supply to the inverter. To obtain Unity Power Factor (UPF) operation of the rectifier, two-loop cascaded control topology is used, where outer loop is implemented by Proportional-Integral (PI) controller and the inner loop is designed by Proportional-Resonant (PR) controller. Different case studies have been observed from the simulink environment pertaining both constant torque and constant power region of motor operation. The efficiency of PMSM has been found above 90% and the rectifier efficiency above 95% accordingly. It is also noted that the motor power factor is improved with gradual increase in load torque and input power factor of the rectifier remains at unity. Along with that, Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of input current is maintained at satisfactory value.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fetal Development Assessment via Contour Detection and CRL Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Accurate fetal growth evaluation is critical for monitoring pregnancy health and delivering appropriate prenatal treatment. We provide a unique strategy for improving the precision of fetal growth assessment by merging sophisticated contour recognition algorithms with Crown-Rump Length (CRL) estimate in this work. We establish a more complete and reliable approach of measuring fetal growth and development by integrating cutting-edge computer vision and deep learning methods. Our technique uses powerful image processing methods to determine the shape of the fetal anatomy in ultrasound images, overcoming hurdles such as noise, artifacts, and fetal positional fluctuations. Following contour identification, exact CRL length estimate is performed, which is a critical predictor of gestational age and fetal well-being. The combination of these two components considerably improves accuracy of fetal growth assessment.

articleTitle: Compensation of any Stable Plants with a Fractional Order PIλDμ Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: A simple design strategy based on root locus technique for the design of fractional order (FO) $P I^{\lambda} D^{\mu}$ controllers has been illustrated in details in this work. This controller has extra tuning parameters and a flexible wide span for their selection to compensate a plant to attain robust stability. After a detail study it is found in many available literatures that FO $P I^{\lambda} D^{\mu}$ controllers are quite preferred, the performance of which is predominant than the integer-order (IO) counter parts, in particular in many applications of servo system control. The limited industrial use of the IO-PID controller and the verified capability of the equivalent non-integer form justifies in its timely interest. In this present work, therefore, numerical examples are illustrated to validate the design approach made with MATLAB simulation results. (126 Words)

articleTitle: Determining Maximum Rooftop Solar Penetration to Mitigate Voltage Swelling in Small-Scale Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) installations play a crucial role in advancing PV penetration within distribution systems. Solar plants on rooftops, particularly those without energy storage, emerge as a cost-effective alternative when compared to conventional fossil fuel-based generation. However, as the proportion of solar PV within a distribution system increases, concerns about voltage swelling arise, especially under lightly loaded conditions. This issue becomes more pronounced in underground cable-based distribution systems due to their high R/X ratio, potentially leading to the curtailment of solar PV generation.In this work, we developed an IEEE 33-bus distribution system in MATLAB to assess the maximum allowable rooftop PV penetration without violating voltage limits. The same IEEE 33-bus network was then modified into a cable-based distribution system to investigate voltage swelling effects. In a comparative analysis between cable-based and overhead-based IEEE 33 bus systems, we found that the maximum allowable rooftop PV penetration is lower in cable-based networks. Simulation results suggest that blindly increasing rooftop PV penetration in a metropolitan cable-based system may lead to voltage instability. Careful planning is essential to ensure the sustainable integration of PV systems without compromising network stability.

articleTitle: A High Precision Fast Capacitive Sensor for Respiratory Moisture Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Humidity sensing in human breath is important for analyzing pulmonary function. The humidity present in the breath of a healthy person during inhalation and exhalation varies from 49% RH to 90% RH. The value below 49% RH indicates unhealthy conditions such as dehydration, irritation in the nasal passage, dry coughing, asthma, and other respiratory issues. Over the years efforts have been made to develop a user-friendly cost-effective point-of-care sensing technology working on different principles including resistive, capacitive, ultrasonic, and optical for respiratory humidity measurement. However, these devices have some demerits like low sensitivity, long response and recovery time, and inconvenience for use. This paper reports the development of a flexible semi-cylindrical capacitive cigarette-like sensor for respiration humidity monitoring. The sensor works on the principle of change in capacitance value because of the humidity in the human breath during inhalation and exhalation. The sensitivity of the sensor is 11.4 fF /10% RH in the 50% - 90% RH range and the recovery time of the sensor is 33 ms. The sensor is highly precise, fast $(\lt1\mathrm{s})$, convenient to use and inexpensive.

articleTitle: Moisture Content Estimation of Nanofluids using LFD of Real and Imaginary Parts of Complex Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper presents the estimation of moisture content of different nanofluids with Low Frequency Dispersion of real and imaginary parts of complex capacitance. For this purpose, nanofluids were prepared in the laboratory with mineral oil as base oil and TiO$_{2} or Al_{2}O_{3}$ nanoparticles. In recent times, condition of the insulating medium has been monitored employing polarization and depolarization current (PDC), return voltage measurements (RVM) and frequency domain spectroscopic (FDS) measurement. In this study, FDS measurement of the nanofluids has been conducted. From the FDS result, complex capacitance has been evaluated. Again the effect of moisture on the complex capacitance have been investigated. Moreover, LFD of real and imaginary parts of complex capacitance has been chosen to estimate the moisture content.

articleTitle: A charge-balancing voltage-to-frequency converter in a 180 nm CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper presents a highly accurate temperature-compensated charge-balancing voltage-to-frequency converter designed in a 180 nm CMOS process. The output frequency of our circuit varies over a range of 2 MHz for an (negative) input range of 3.3 V. The circuit exhibits less than 0.016% nonlinearity error while consuming a power of 2mW. The output frequency of our circuit exhibits a variation of 220 ppm over $0-100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ after minimizing the temperature coefficient of the resistors used. The sensitivity of the VFC can be varied by changing the clock frequency of the comparator and a reference current.

articleTitle: Pore Morphology Study of Porous Electrodes Using Eddy Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: Porous electrodes are used for the fabrication of different vapour-sensors including capacitive and resistive sensors. The capacitive sensors in Shaw Moisture Meter, UK, use porous gold electrodes for moisture detection in gases. The porous electrodes play an important role in the sensing performance parameters of a thin film/thick sensor. At present, costly analytical instruments are used to study the pore morphology of porous materials. This paper introduces a novel eddy current sensor for investigating the pore morphology of metal electrodes. The sensor is designed and simulated using COMSOL Multiphysics software for the most commonly used interdigital electrodes with various pore sizes. Finally, the sensor is fabricated and experimentally validated using a Keysight LCR meter at 100 kHz. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method offering a valuable non-destructive testing technique for analyzing the pore morphology of the porous electrode (sensitivity 0.9 H/mm).

articleTitle: Cost-benefit analysis of rooftop solar at a multi-storied commercial building in Newtown, Kolkata
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
abstract: This paper aims to evaluate the performance of a grid-connected rooftop solar plant on a commercial building situated at Newtown, Kolkata. In this paper, the annual energy consumption of the studied building is estimated through the eQUEST 3.65 building energy simulation tool, and the generation of solar power corresponding to rooftop PV at the exact building location is evaluated through PVsyst and a detailed cost-benefit analysis has been done for the same rooftop solar project, having the installed capacity of 125 kWp.

articleTitle: Realization of Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation Scheme for a Quasi Z-Source Inverter in FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Control, Instrumentation, Energy & Communication (CIEC)
